method.summary: AISim's own Weka lowering, not a reimplementation: an 81-line Rust CLI (WT benchmarks/learned_routing/tools/agentx_lower) calls the public aisimulate_core::replay::loadgen::WekaImporter (=0.13.0-dev.202609300000000061, the crate the bindings link; helper Cargo.lock pins the same serde_json 1.0.150, blake3 1.8.7) to emit each capped play's header and rows once (base rows). Python (learned_routing.workloads.agentx_lowered) only recycles: draws copies per split, prefixes ids, remaps hash ids to disjoint per-copy ranges, sets ordinals, and in open mode rebases not_before_ms to Poisson play arrivals.
method.input_plays: 82 selected plays (traces/agentx/plays) after B2's AgentX transforms: the plain cap (think_cap_s=300, max_model_len=131072) in traces/agentx_lowered/weka_cap300/<play>.json, plus think_mult 0.5/2/4 and osl_mult 1.5/2.5 on top of it in weka_cap300_<think|osl><m>/ (fix_r0); each byte-identical to the play lines inside B2's AgentX cell traces that use the same transform (transforms.by_tag.*.b2_cell_trace_check)
hash_namespace_semantics: native: ns = 'weka:' + blake3(relative source name)[:16]; source name = path relative to the corpus root, or '<file>#<line:06>' inside .jsonl; ids are '{ns}:request:<source id>', '{ns}:session:<stream>', '{ns}:play:<trace id>'

native: full 64-token block with source hash h -> u64_le(blake3('weka-full-block\0source:{name}:{h}\0{nonce}')[:8]): the (relative path, source hash) pair is the identity, nonce resolves u64 collisions within one play
native: missing source hash -> 'private:missing:{request_id}:{i}'; partial tail block -> 'weka-partial-tail\0{request_id}:{blocks}:{input_length}' (request-private)

native: header hash_id_scope='local' but replay interns u64 ids GLOBALLY in node order (WorkloadDriver: dense u32 by first appearance), so isolation between plays comes only from the per-play namespace

recycled: copy i maps the k-th distinct id of its play (first appearance in row order) to hash_base_i + k; ranges [hash_base_i, hash_base_i + distinct_i) are consecutive from 1 and disjoint, so equal source hashes stay equal within a copy and never collide across copies or plays; engine re-chunking 64 -> 16 tokens runs on synthesized tokens exactly as for native Weka
recycling_semantics: copy i draws pool[index_draw(seed, 'agentx-lowered-draw|' + split, i, len(pool))] (blake2b counter draw, with replacement) from the split's sorted pool only
ids: 'lrx:{i:06d}:' + native id for request_id, session_id, play_id and every dependency target; subagent session structure and within-play sort order unchanged
source_play_ordinal = i (contiguous); replay sorts plays by ordinal and deals lanes ordinal % agentic_lanes, so lane j runs copies j, j+L, j+2L, ... back to back
dependency edges (relation, trigger, delay_ms), lengths, models, recorded_api_time_ms copied verbatim
closed: not_before_ms unchanged (lanes rebase each play to its activation: start + max(nb - root_nb, 0))

open: not_before_ms = a_i + max(nb - root_nb, 0) on every row (the lane rebase at a_i; descendants keep offsets, which replay uses as floors under dependency times); a_0 = 0, a_i = a_{i-1} - ln(1 - u_i)/rate, u_i = unit_draw(seed, 'agentx-lowered-arrival', i), rounded to whole ns; independent of split and rate

header: schema dynamo.agentic_mooncake v2, block_size 64 and hash_id_scope local copied from the base rows; source = {format: weka, digest: lr-agentx-lowered-v1:<spec key>} (provenance only; replay ignores it)

graph_digests.what: for every play, the canonical graph digest (blake3 over all compiled nodes: ids, lengths, hash ids, not_before_ms, dependencies) of native load_weka_agentic_graph equals that of AgenticTrace::from_agentic_mooncake(base file) Repeated for each of the six play transforms (fix_r0): 82/82 equal for each.

tiers.single: each play alone: native capped Weka file vs base agentic file (ids identical) and vs a relabeled copy (lrx prefix and new hash range, ids mapped back); timestamp mode
tiers.corpus: the 6 plays as one native directory vs its AISim lowering vs relabeled copies ordered like the native ids; timestamp mode and agentic_lanes 2 and 3
tiers.recycle: 12 seeded draws with replacement from the 6 plays (5 distinct): native directory with one file per copy (distinct names = native copy isolation) vs this module's recycling with disjoint hash ranges and native-ordered labels; timestamp mode and agentic_lanes 3 and 5 (lanes run 2-4 copies each)

replay.coverage: explicit subagents (0098: 1 subagent lowered to 19 streams; 0073: 6; 0390: 5; 0013: 3), joins, replay barriers, spawn/dispatch (concurrent, non-blocking children: 0073 has 5, 0315 has 4 detected streams without a subagent marker), spawn/completion, and the only authored zero-output request (0021). No selected play has an async_launched (background) subagent, so that importer branch is not exercised by data.
replay.wording_correction_fix_r0: audit parity-fidelity r0 m1: the single tier ran in timestamp mode only (agentic_lanes null in all 48 single cases); only the corpus (lanes 2, 3) and recycle (lanes 3, 5) tiers also ran lanes. The STATE.md line of 16:47 overstated this. The builder's exact cases replayed relabeled files with base headers and native-ordered labels, never an unmodified generator file; the auditor closed that gap with unmodified generator output (64/64 single copies, 24/24 two-play cases, 36/36 untouched 12-copy prefixes; audits/agentx-lowering/parity-fidelity-r0.md rows 6-8).

node_order_sensitivity.what: the same 12-copy recycled corpus with this module's default labels (copy index order) instead of native-ordered labels
node_order_sensitivity.explanation: replay sorts nodes by request_id; node order breaks ties between simultaneously ready requests (ReadySession session_index) and fixes the dense u32 hash interning. Native order follows blake3 of file names; the generator uses copy index. Neither is privileged; the effect is the same kind as a crn-order-v1 replicate. In this worst case all lanes start at t = 0; open-mode Poisson arrivals rarely tie.

parity_evidence.open_mode_semantics_check: validate runs check every root becomes ready exactly at its copy's arrival and no request is ready before it (runs[*].open_mode_arrivals)

generator_usage.build_base_once: cd WT/benchmarks/learned_routing/tools/agentx_lower && cargo build --release --offline; PY -m learned_routing.workloads.agentx_lowered build-base --all-cell-transforms (or one transform: build-base [--think-cap-s S] [--think-mult M] [--osl-mult M])
generator_usage.open: PY -m learned_routing.workloads.agentx_lowered --split {train|val|test} --mode open --num-copies C --seed K --play-rate-per-s R_TOTAL [--out PATH]   (R_TOTAL = per-worker play rate x N; C >= R_TOTAL x (warm-up + window + margin))
generator_usage.closed: PY -m learned_routing.workloads.agentx_lowered --split S --mode closed --num-copies C --seed K [--out PATH]; replay with agentic_lanes = lanes per worker x N and C >= 8 x lanes
generator_usage.output: PATH (default traces/agentx_lowered/gen/<sha256>.jsonl) plus PATH.meta.json (spec, draws, per-copy label/hash range/start, sha256)
generator_usage.replay_call: run_trace_replay(path, trace_format='agentic_mooncake', execution_model='Qwen/Qwen3-32B', arrival_speedup_ratio=1.0 (a speedup also divides think/tool delays), agentic_lanes=L for closed mode, trace_block_size ignored (header 64))
generator_usage.python_api: agentx_lowered.GenSpec(...); write_generated(spec, root, out) -> meta; generate(spec, root) -> (header, rows, meta) without writing
generator_usage.crn_replicates: harness replicates.py (crn-order-v1) does not handle agentic_mooncake. Suggested replicate k for a lowered cell: the same GenSpec with seed = k (new draws and arrivals, shared by every policy). Files at the same seed share draws across N and modes (same copy count -> identical draws) and normalized arrivals across rates.
generator_usage.harness_gap: learned_routing.cells.Cell.load_kwargs accepts agentic_lanes only for trace_format weka, and replicates.materialize_replicate rejects agentic_mooncake; calibration must extend both (not edited here by rule).
generator_usage.parity_and_validation: PY -m learned_routing.workloads.agentx_lowered parity; PY -m learned_routing.workloads.agentx_lowered validate --runs-json RUNS --out-dir DIR [--keep-per-request]
generator_usage.transform_cells: add --think-mult M or --osl-mult M (GenSpec think_mult/osl_mult) to the open/closed command; PlayTransform.from_cell(cell['transform']) gives the values; meta.json records spec.think_mult/osl_mult and transform {think_cap_s, think_mult, osl_mult, max_model_len, tag}
generator_usage.parity_per_transform: PY -m learned_routing.workloads.agentx_lowered parity --think-mult M | --osl-mult M [--out-dir DIR]

suggested_loads.status: suggestion only; calibration finalizes loads and the AgentX SLA with the A2 band rule (default good_frac about 0.95/0.85/0.65 at L1/L2/L3)
suggested_loads.how_measured: default = dynamo-default-cost-fn seed 1; train pool; A2 good fraction in the steady window (open: arrival basis; closed: completion basis) on a grid of provisional SLAs; E0 = ais-chunked-estimator-v1. Points and interpolations: validation.band_tables; every run: validation.runs[*].good_frac

provisional_sla.why: the integration stage's provisional SLA; at L1/L2 loads (closed lanes <= 5, open <= 0.002 plays/s per worker) adding E2E slowdown 3 to I = 40 ms changes good_frac by <= 0.004, at closed L3 by up to 0.041, so ITL sets the band

alternative_at_I30_S3_interpolated.note: linear interpolation between measured lanes 3..6 (hypothesis until measured)

closed_mode.copies: >= 8 x lanes (window 2,460-10,620 s simulated in these runs); each extra copy per lane lengthens the window by about one play sojourn (1,770-2,660 s measured)
closed_mode.warmup: p90 over lanes of the end of each lane's first copy: 3,300-4,920 s simulated in the 15 closed runs
closed_mode.window_end: first lane out of copies (7,380-14,880 s at 8 copies per lane)
closed_mode.steady_state: stationary in all 16 closed runs (lanes 2-6, N 8/16/32, default and round robin, train and val); in-flight plays = lanes by construction; per-worker active requests 0.5-3.4; telemetry active KV usage 0.12-0.72

open_mode.play_rate_per_s: per_worker_rate x N (generator --play-rate-per-s takes the total)
open_mode.cliff: between 0.002 and 0.0025 plays/s per worker the open system loses its steady state at every N: play stretch (sojourn / recorded span) and in-flight plays keep growing (N32 at 0.0025: in-flight drift 1.40, stretch 1.28 -> 1.79 by third; N8 at 0.003: stretch 4.2, good_frac 0.004). The A2 L3 target (0.65) therefore has no stationary open-loop load at I40_S3 or I30_S3; use closed lanes for L3, or accept a drifting window.
open_mode.why_I_matters: with a tighter ITL (I = 25 ms, about 1.35x the light-load ITL p50 of 18.3-18.7 ms) the stable rates 0.0015/0.002 sit near 0.95/0.85, which keeps open-loop L1/L2 off the cliff
open_mode.copies: rate x N x (warm-up + window + margin); 16,000 s of arrivals was used
open_mode.warmup: Little's-law plateau of in-flight plays: 1,500-2,880 s simulated at stable loads (later and non-stationary near the cliff)
open_mode.steady_state: stationary at 0.0015 and 0.002 for N 8/16/32 (train); N16 test pool at 0.002 flagged (in-flight drift 0.81 against tolerance 0.16, flat stretch 1.18-1.21); N8 at 0.001 flagged from small counts (13 plays in flight, flat stretch)

suggested_loads.lr12_note: closed-mode bands are nearly N-invariant at matched lanes per worker (N8/16/32 within 0.03 except L3 0.64-0.71); open mode is N-dependent past 0.002 (N32 tolerates more than N8). Calibrate per N as LR-12 says, and expect knee-matched open loads to differ by N.
suggested_loads.transform_cells: not covered by the closed/open suggestions above (measured on cap300 only). Provisional paired runs (transforms.validation): think 0.5 is stationary at 3 lanes/worker (N4) and drifts at 4-5; think 2 and 4 are light at 4-5 lanes/worker; osl 1.5/2.5 stay stationary at 5 lanes/worker with default good 0.825/0.862 (I40 S3). Calibration sets each transform cell's load with the A2 band rule.

steady_state_rules.window_end: open: last play arrival; closed: first lane out of copies
steady_state_rules.warmup_open: first 60 s bin whose 5-bin trailing mean of in-flight plays reaches 90% of the median bin over the second half of [0, window end)
steady_state_rules.warmup_closed: p90 over lanes of the end of each lane's first copy (all lanes start in phase at t = 0)
steady_state_rules.stationary: |last third / first third - 1| <= max(0.15, 2 / sqrt(level x third/sojourn)) on in-flight plays (open) or requests (closed)

costs.base_build_s: about 7 s for all 82 plays (lowering, two digests per play)
costs.generate_note: seconds for generate() and serialization in one process; files are about 8.5 KB per row (64-token hash ids); 56K rows = 474 MB
costs.transform_base_build_s: 41.4 s wall for all six transforms (82 plays each, lowering plus two digests per play; runs/agentx_lowered/fix_r0/build_base.log)

caveats: Node order is a free choice the lowering cannot pin: replay sorts nodes by request_id, which breaks ties between simultaneously ready requests and fixes the dense u32 hash interning. Native corpora order plays by blake3 of file names; the generator orders copies by index. Exact parity needs the native order (parity uses label_ranks); in the generator's own order the 12-copy recycled corpus differed in 12/12 replays, mean e2e -7.4% to +4.7% (worst case: synchronized start). This is the same class of variation as a crn-order-v1 replicate, not a lowering error.

Lowered plays are B2's transformed plays (think_cap_s = 300 s, plus think_mult or osl_mult for the 5 transform cells), byte-identical to the AgentX cell traces that use the same transform, not the raw plays. Each transform has its own weka_<tag>/base_<tag>; a transform cell generated from base_cap300 would replay untransformed traffic, which GenSpec prevents (the base MANIFEST must match the spec's transform).

No selected play has an async_launched (background) subagent, so that importer branch is not exercised by data; dispatch-triggered spawns (concurrent children) and the only zero-output request are covered by parity.

Open mode makes play roots exogenous (Poisson). Descendants keep the native semantics: ready at max(recorded offset from the play start, dependency completion + delay_ms), so a descendant never starts before its recorded offset (causal release per LR-09, with recorded floors).

The suggested loads use a provisional SLA (I = 40 ms, S = 3) and the train pool; val (N16 lanes 4: 0.937 vs train 0.951) and test (N16 open 0.002: 0.971 vs train 0.962) pools respond slightly differently. The full SLA grid is in every run record.
Steady-state rules (warm-up, window end, stationarity tolerance) are heuristics for calibration to adopt or replace; stationarity flags at N = 8 and low load are limited by Poisson noise.

Harness integration is not done here (by rule): learned_routing.cells.Cell.load_kwargs accepts agentic_lanes only for trace_format weka, replicates.materialize_replicate rejects agentic_mooncake, and cells.expected_cost_s estimates non-Mooncake files as 5 s + size / 5 MB (474 MB -> about 100 s vs 224 s measured; the pool timeout max(120 s, 20 x cost) still covers it).
Files are about 8.5 KB per row (one 64-token hash id per block); N = 32 traces are 220-475 MB. Generation takes about 6 s per 56K rows, so calibration can regenerate instead of keeping files.

Replay costs 2.9-4.9 ms per row in one fresh process at N 8-32 (startup included): AgentX N = 32 lanes cells take 2-4 minutes per replay at 8 copies per lane, N = 8 cells 20-50 s; size CMA-ES budgets accordingly.

The base manifest sha changed after the validation traces were generated (the helper was rebuilt after cargo fmt; all 82 base files stayed byte-identical, runs/agentx_lowered/base_shas_before_fmt.json): validation trace headers embed manifest sha 0a032304..., the current one is 9868b9f6....
Header source is {format: weka, digest: lr-agentx-lowered-v1:<spec key>}; replay only checks it is non-empty.
per_request arrival_time_ms of a non-root request is its release (ready) time, not a trace timestamp.

Node-order sensitivity grows with output length: the 12-copy synchronized recycled corpus in copy-index order moved mean e2e by -5.7..+18.0% (osl 1.5) and -15.6..+13.5% (osl 2.5), vs -7.4..+4.7% (cap300), -6.8..+2.8% (think 0.5), -2.6..+5.4% (think 2) and -0.1..+0.7% (think 4). This is a synchronized-start N = 2 worst case and the same class as a crn-order-v1 replicate; measure lowered-cell noise with seed = k replicates (A1) per transform.

think_mult dilates every recorded gap of the play (think, tool and api time, subagent durations) about its first request; in closed mode it therefore changes the offered load per lane, so transform cells cannot reuse the base cells' lanes (transforms.validation.observations).

transforms.what: B2's AgentX cells use six per-play Weka transforms (transform.transform_weka): the plain cap (think_cap_s 300) and think_mult 0.5/2/4 or osl_mult 1.5/2.5 on top of it. Each is lowered by AISim into its own weka_<tag>/base_<tag> directories with its own 82-play graph-digest proof and a byte check against every B2 cell trace that uses it. A transformed AgentX cell MUST be generated from its own transform's base (GenSpec think_mult/osl_mult); the generator refuses a base built for another transform and fails loudly when a transform has no base.
transforms.added_in: fix_r0 (audit parity-fidelity r0 F1), WT commit <commit-13>
transforms.cell_to_spec: t = PlayTransform.from_cell(cell['transform']) (rejects window/isl_*/prefix_root_mult/max_model_len != 131072); GenSpec(split=cell['split'], mode=..., num_copies=..., seed=k, play_rate_per_s=..., think_cap_s=t.think_cap_s, think_mult=t.think_mult, osl_mult=t.osl_mult). CLI: --think-mult M / --osl-mult M
transforms.draws_independent_of_transform: draws, labels, ordinals, hash ranges and open-mode arrivals depend only on split, num_copies, seed (and rate), so a transformed spec replays the same plays in the same order as its identity twin (tested: test_think_mult_dilates_every_copy_and_nothing_else)

think_mult changes the offered load per lane (it dilates think and tool gaps, and api time): at the identity-level lanes, think 2 (N8, 4 lanes/worker) and think 4 (N4, 5 lanes/worker) are light (busy 0.70 / 0.50, default good 0.993 / 0.990 at I40 S3), and think 0.5 at 5 lanes/worker is past the stationary limit (in-flight drift 1.49 > tolerance 0.41, good 0.575); think 0.5 is stationary at 3 lanes/worker (good 0.972) and drifts at 4 (1.69 > 0.50, good 0.846)
osl_mult at the identity-level lanes stays stationary: osl 1.5 N4 5 lanes/worker good 0.825 vs identity 0.842; osl 2.5 N8 5 lanes/worker good 0.862 vs identity 0.885 (I40 S3)
so the transform cells need their own load calibration (A2 band rule per cell); the base cells' suggested lanes do not carry over to think_mult cells
